messages.author: a387d7985c232d82
messages.subject: StanProgress.txt gone
parts:
Dear all,

I am currently estimating a long-running Stan model using rstan version 2.9.0-3 on my late-2013 Mac Pro. Initially, the progress file ("...ProgressStan.txt") opened automatically in Safari as usual. However, after a few days, the ProgressStan.txt seems to have disappeared: Safari can't reload the file, and I can't find in anywhere on my computer. Any thoughts on what might have happened and how I might check the progress of my model in other ways? Thanks!

Devin

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: StanProgress.txt gone
parts:
On Wednesday, April 6, 2016 at 11:51:01 AM UTC-4, Devin Caughey wrote:
I am currently estimating a long-running Stan model using rstan version 2.9.0-3 on my late-2013 Mac Pro. Initially, the progress file ("...ProgressStan.txt") opened automatically in Safari as usual. However, after a few days, the ProgressStan.txt seems to have disappeared: Safari can't reload the file, and I can't find in anywhere on my computer. Any thoughts on what might have happened and how I might check the progress of my model in other ways? Thanks!

If R is still running, then it should be in the temporary directory for the R session. On a Mac / Linux, that would be under /tmp somewhere. On Windows, it is usually under My Documents/App Data/ or something. But R deletes that temporary directly when you quit R.

Ben

messages.author: 3b4499f4bb9ae5a3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: StanProgress.txt gone
parts:
Thanks Ben,

R is still running, but the folder that once contained the progress file (/var/folders/67/k5k525tx2r39f09_y5zj7cbw0000gn/T/RtmpxSOXVX/) now contains only an empty folder called “devtools2fb3137fe15”. Looks like something must have deleted the progress file. Anyway, probably nothing can be done about it, but if you have any ideas about how to monitor progress let me know. Would re-creating the file manually work, I wonder?

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: StanProgress.txt gone
parts:
On Thursday, April 7, 2016 at 12:59:40 PM UTC-4, Devin Caughey wrote:
I’m running four parallel chains and all seem to be still running. Is there any way to know whether they are not just caught in some infinite loop?

Not unless you happened to call stan with the sample_file argument. But there are few, if any, while loops in the Stan Math library, so it is probably just taking a lot of very small steps.

Ben

messages.author: 3b4499f4bb9ae5a3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] StanProgress.txt gone
parts:
Hello all,

To follow up, setting open_progress = FALSE worked (i.e., printed progress to the console). However, I subsequently encountered another, possibly related problem involving the parallel package. After running Stan for several days (a short run doesn’t yield this problem), I encounter the following fatal error after all Stan chains have finished:
Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) : 
  4 nodes produced errors; first error: cannot open the connection
Warning message:
In file(file, "r") :
  cannot open file '/var/folders/67/k5k525tx2r39f09_y5zj7cbw0000gn/T//Rtmpck6AID/file9e1424c1bc2': No such file or directory

For the record, checkForRemoteErrors is from the parallel package and is defined thusly:
function (val) {
    count <- 0
    firstmsg <- NULL
    for (v in val) {
        if (inherits(v, "try-error")) {
            count <- count + 1
            if (count == 1) 
                firstmsg <- v
        }
    }
    if (count == 1) 
        stop("one node produced an error: ", firstmsg, domain = NA)
    else if (count > 1) 
        stop(count, " nodes produced errors; first error: ", 
            firstmsg, domain = NA)
    val
}

I suspect that what is happening here is that parallel (like rstan when open_progress = TRUE) creates a temporary file in the var directory that is being deleted sometime during the Stan run. So when checkForRemoteErrors looks for the file after Stan is finished, it can’t find it. Perhaps some program of mine is periodically “cleaning up” the var folder. If anyone has an ideas about what is going on, I would love to hear it. I am running a Mac Pro (Late 2013) with El Capitan.

Devin

Another follow-up, this time with an apparent solution. Instead of writing the progress files to /var/folders/…, I specified an alternative location by running the following command:
Sys.setenv(TMPDIR = "~/R-Output/tmp")
This seemed to work, in that rstan finished without incident.
